headline: Fourth-quarter growth caps a leaner, more profitable year
summary_short: Q4 net sales rose 6% to $3.63B (5% organic), the GAAP net loss narrowed to $116M from $546M, and adjusted diluted EPS jumped to $0.39 from $0.09, as easing impairment charges offset $293M of restructuring costs.
summary_long: Q4 net sales rose 6% (5% organic) to $3.63B, growing in every region and all categories but Hair Care, led by Skin Care and a 12% Mainland China rebound. GAAP operating loss narrowed to $39M from $390M as last year's $425M impairment did not repeat, despite $293M of PRGP restructuring charges this quarter. Adjusted operating income rose 95% to $267M; adjusted diluted EPS rose to $0.39 from $0.09. Full-year gross margin expanded 150bp and free cash flow nearly doubled to $1.32B; cash rose to $3.50B. For fiscal 2027, the company affirmed 3%-5% organic sales growth and raised its adjusted operating margin outlook to 12.7%-13.5% from 12.5%-13.0%.

drivers.explanation: A fourth straight quarter of accelerating organic growth, plus the absence of last year's $425M intangible impairment, narrowed the operating loss and lifted adjusted profitability, even as $293M of restructuring charges continued.
Growth was broad-based across every region and all categories except Hair Care, led by Skin Care and a rebound in Mainland China; an $18M gift-card liability reversal also helped the Americas.
Margin expansion reflects PRGP procurement and expense-optimization benefits plus a $38M IEEPA tariff-refund benefit in cost of sales, partly offset by incremental tariffs and inflation.
The loss narrowed mainly because last year's quarter included a $425M intangible impairment that did not recur; restructuring charges rose to $293M from $106M, partly offsetting the improvement.
PRGP-driven operating leverage and gross-margin expansion funded a 7% increase in consumer-facing investment while non-consumer-facing costs stayed roughly flat.
Net loss narrowed in step with the smaller operating loss, though the effective tax rate rose to 64.8% from (8.9)% on foreign valuation-allowance changes and new U.S. tax legislation.
Full-year operating cash flow rose 39% on higher net earnings, while capex fell to $457M from $602M, driving free cash flow growth.

confidence_notes: FORCE-REGENERATE mode was requested by the operator for this run; note that no prior EL_US_FY2026_Q2 summary file existed on disk, so this is a fresh compose rather than a true overwrite. Data-quality finding (consistent with the same issue already flagged on the FY2026 Q1 summary): this event is stored under period label 'FY2026 Q2' on the shard, but the underlying filing (EX-99.1, filed 2026-08-19) explicitly reports 'Fiscal 2026 Fourth Quarter and Full Year' results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 — i.e. this is fiscal Q4 / full-year, not fiscal Q2. Estee Lauder's fiscal year begins July 1, so a June 30 quarter-end is fiscal Q4; the shard appears to label periods via calendar-quarter arithmetic on the report-end date (Mar-end -> Q1, Jun-end -> Q2, Sep-end -> Q3, Dec-end -> Q4) rather than the company's actual fiscal-quarter numbering — the fiscal-offset-issuer bug class documented in this repo's CLAUDE.md. This summary is filed under the shard's existing period label ('FY2026 Q2') to preserve the event/summary join, but every KPI and the narrative above describe the real fiscal Q4 / full-year results. The mislabeling doesn't affect sequencing, so q/q and y/y deltas against the adjacent shard events (labeled 'FY2026 Q1' and 'FY2025 Q2', which are themselves really fiscal Q3 FY2026 and fiscal Q4 FY2025) are valid true-quarter comparisons. q/q figures for Net sales, Gross profit and Cost of sales blend this quarter's SEC-verbatim press-release numbers with the prior quarter's Yahoo fundamentals-timeseries values (confidence 0.85); q/q figures for Operating income, Net income, EPS, cash, and equity use the prior quarter's SEC-verbatim 10-Q values (confidence 0.98) — both same basis (GAAP as-reported). Short-term debt jumped from $3M to $503M year over year; the release does not explain this move (most likely a reclassification of long-term debt to its current portion, not disclosed in this exhibit), so it is presented as a dollar delta rather than the resulting (meaningless, >16,000%) percentage, and no driver cause is asserted. Recommend a dedicated backfill to correct EL's period labels against its real fiscal calendar before further shard diffing on this ticker.
